text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPLOlITA
- Enhancing commercial viability of Poland's sea transport should double the Polish ports' turnover by 2010, according to a development programme of the parliamentary transport committee.

- Poland's KGHM copper combine has not participated in a recent tender for mining the Zaire-based Tenke Fungurume copper seam in the Shaba province, as it is interested in seams located in other parts of the province, a KGHM top executive said.
- The Gdansk authorities will buy 11 buses from Germany's Neoplan for the city's public transport system, Gdansk vice-president Longin Mazewski said.
- Construction and trading company Mostostal Export will increase its stake in the Zamosc-based Delia SA garment maker, which will thus increase it capital.
- Techma Krakow, controlled by the listed KrakChemia, will construct production and trading halls worth six million zlotys for the listed Optimus computer maker by April 1998.
NOWA EUROPA
- The rolling stock modernisation will take PKP, the state-owned railway monopolist, up to five years, the company said.
- Poland's treasury ministry has published a call for tenders, valid until January 17, 1997, for the sale of at least 10 percent of shares of the Dromex road construction firm.
- The employment in Poland's coal mining sector has fallen from 416,000 to 260,000 workers in the past six years, the government said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Germany's Volkswagen AG will take over the remaining 12.22 percent stake in the Volswagen Poznan plant held by the Bank Rozwoju Eksportu (BRE) Export Development Bank by the year-end, Volkswagen said.
- The Wroclaw-based household durable maker Polar has introduced washing machines adapted to the needs of blind invalids. The new product's price is identical with that of the standard version.
- Finland's Primalco, the producer of Finlandia vodka, will distill vodka in cooperation with the Zyrardow-based Polmos company. The vodka brand to be made will not be Finlandia, Primalco said.
ZYCIE
- Around 80 percent of Poles are frustrated with TV advertisements and 71 are bored with them, a recent survey by the CBOS polling institute said.
- Despite previous announcements by the management of the Polisa insurance company, the general shareholders meeting motioned for trading a part of its shares on the over-the-counter (OTC) market.
PARKIET
- Carlsberg's top executives Poul J. Svanholm and Flemming Lindelov have visited the Okocim brewery in southern Poland. Next year the brewery will start brewing Carlsberg beer.
- The listed Pekpol meat processing firm will start trading 448,000 A-series shares, which should raise share prices by 50 percent, the management said.
- The Lodz-based Petrobank will provide the National Investment Fund (NFI) Hetman with two turnover loans worth 33 million zlotys, the bank said.
